title: The generalised semi-Clifford conjecture is false
abstract: The Clifford hierarchy is a nested sequence of sets of quantum gates that can be fault-tolerantly performed using gate teleportation within standard quantum error correction schemes. The importance of these gates has motivated numerous studies of their structure. Zeng-Chen-Chuang conjectured in 2007 that all hierarchy gates are generalised semi-Clifford, i.e. take the form $C_1 ΠD C_2$ for Clifford gates $C_1, C_2$, a permutation gate $Π$, and a diagonal gate $D$; Beigi-Shor proved in 2008 that this holds for all third-level gates.   We construct a five-qubit gate that is in the fifth level of the Clifford hierarchy but is not generalised semi-Clifford. Rather than simply present and verify our counterexample to the generalised semi-Clifford conjecture, we show how its form can be deduced. Our counterexample also demonstrates that the Clifford hierarchy is not closed under inverses.
summary: This theoretical paper disproves the generalized semi-Clifford conjecture concerning quantum gates in the Clifford hierarchy. The authors construct a specific five-qubit gate that is mathematically proven to be in the fifth level of the hierarchy but lacks the required algebraic structure. This finding significantly refines our understanding of the limitations and boundaries of fault-tolerant quantum computation models.
main_problem: The paper aims to disprove the generalized semi-Clifford conjecture, which posits that all gates in the Clifford hierarchy must have a specific algebraic structure.
main_result: The authors construct a concrete five-qubit gate that belongs to the fifth level of the Clifford hierarchy but does not possess the generalized semi-Clifford property. Furthermore, they show the hierarchy is not closed under inverses.
method: The proof uses advanced algebraic techniques involving symplectic linear algebra, Pauli groups, and analyzing the structure of commutators of quantum gates to characterize membership in the hierarchy and the GSC property.
model_or_system: The study concerns quantum gates acting on $n$ qubits, specifically focusing on the structure and properties of the Clifford hierarchy ($\mathcal{C}_k(n)$) within the unitary group $U(\mathcal{H}_n)$.
key_observables: The primary observables are the gate structure itself, the membership level in the Clifford hierarchy ($\mathcal{C}_k$), and the existence of a common invariant Lagrangian for the associated Pauli algebras.
important_parameters: The number of qubits ($n=5$ for the counterexample) and the level of the hierarchy ($k=5$) are crucial parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis proceeds by developing equivalent characterizations for hierarchy membership and the GSC property, building upon established results for lower-level gates.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the five-qubit counterexample circuit, which is constructed using controlled-Clifford gates.
paper_structure: The paper develops the necessary algebraic machinery to characterize the Clifford hierarchy and the GSC property, then constructs a specific five-qubit unitary gate that satisfies the hierarchy condition but violates the GSC condition, concluding with a proof that the gate's inverse also falls outside the hierarchy.
why_interesting: This work provides deep structural insights into the limitations of gate sets used in quantum error correction and computation, revealing that the assumed algebraic constraints (GSC) are too restrictive for the full complexity of the Clifford hierarchy.
